usage: This is the standard, secular way to say hello in Modern Standard Arabic. It is used in formal writing, news broadcasts, and educational settings, and is appropriate for addressing anyone regardless of gender or number. While 'as-salamu 3alaykum' is also ubiquitous, 'mar7aban' is the most direct equivalent to a simple English hello.

variants.label: formal greeting
variants.note: The most common formal and traditional greeting used across the Arab world.

variants.label: casual / short
variants.note: A shorter, slightly more casual greeting often used interchangeably with marhaban.

variants.label: warm welcome
variants.note: Used when receiving guests or emphasizing a warm reception.

examples.english: Hello, how are you today? (to a man)
She said hello, then sat down.
